ops.entry: WHEN a plan deletes or changes behaviour, or every criterion passes, DO grade the affirmative present-tense claims in signed prose against measured behaviour: the plan's text and each kept decision's whole entry, not only its policy clause. No criterion quantifies over them, so an overclaim survives panels and goal-checks.
ops.why: Sharpens P-16 to plan time: a 'no decision amendments' scope collided with a kept decision whose present-tense implementation sentence the planned deletion falsified; same rule, wider reach, same length.
Displaced: byte-for-byte preservation criteria are rare and narrow; the external-payload field enumeration rule cost three validate rounds and an operator escalation this feature.

ops.entry: WHEN a criterion declares what counts as valid or absent in an external payload DO enumerate every field the decision reads, plus the identity binding of related objects, in the criterion and again as per-field graded evidence; container-shape cases alone let each later round surface one more unvalidated field.
ops.why: Three validate rounds each found the next unvalidated field of one payload class; the last fell outside the signed criterion with rework budget spent. Goal-check evidence citing only container cases graded met wrongly.
Displaced: a runner swallowing a production-only flag is a narrow tooling trap; losing a writer receipt forced an operator ruling on the record itself.

ops.entry: WHEN a writer's stdout is the evidence of what it did DO capture it whole into a durable path inside your write grant as it runs: a temp file vanishes and printed prefixes truncate, and re-running a writer to recover it records a different run.
ops.why: Apply step redirected writer stdout to a temp file and printed 300-char prefixes; the temp dir vanished, leaving only a truncated receipt the operator had to rule on.

ops.entry: WHEN proving a verify is red on the unbuilt tree DO read where the red arises, not the status: a missing argument exits 2, a diff over a self-edited file is red while uncommitted, and an earlier failure point reddens before the one the task names. Each mimics discrimination.
ops.why: A fail-first gap was closed by a red from a pre-loop failure rather than the per-item failure the signed task named; generalizes O-13's mimic list at equal length.

originals.original: WHEN every criterion passes DO still grade the approved plan's affirmative prose claims against measured behaviour: an overclaim inside signed prose is quantified over by no criterion, so it survives a plan panel and every goal-check.

WHEN a signed criterion requires text to move byte-for-byte DO compare the pinned baseline bytes directly and keep any new explanation in separate prose; semantic equivalence or adjacency cannot discharge literal preservation.

WHEN a planned verify passes a production-only flag through a test runner DO inspect the runner's argument handling and invoke the production entrypoint directly; an ignored flag leaves the ordinary suite green without exercising the required gate.

WHEN proving a verify discriminates by requiring non-zero on the unbuilt tree DO read the message, not just the status: a script invoked without its required argument exits 2, and a diff over a file the task itself edits is red while uncommitted. Both mimic discrimination.

ops.entry: WHEN sizing or amending a task DO count its machine-field lines against the 50-line per-task cap first: amend accepts an over-cap task and only plan-merge check or check-plan-routes.py fails it, and intent is not counted, so derive a long file list inside verify from plan.yaml rather than inlining it.
ops.why: An amend adding files and verify lines tipped a task to 53 lines, caught only at check; a literal file list in a verify heredoc blew the cap. Sharpens G-03 with the amend blind spot and the remedy.

originals.original: WHEN sizing a task for `check-plan-routes.py` DO count the `files:` list first: machine fields are capped at 50 lines per task and `intent:` is not counted, so a long file list steals the room `verify:` needs.
